profile.name: Lamia Islam
profile.headline: ICE Graduate, Pabna University of Science and Technology
profile.contactNote: I am looking for PhD positions starting in 2027 in safe and inclusive AI: systems, from adaptive learning tools to robots and vehicles, that read people, know when that reading might be wrong, and act with care when it is. Email is the best way to reach me.

about.lede: My research centres on reliable, interpretable and inclusive AI for systems that interact with people.
paragraphs: I have long been curious about why people perceive and respond to the same situation so differently. In AI, this becomes a practical question: how a model forms its judgement of a person, when that judgement can be trusted, and how the system should act when it cannot.
My work spans physiological signal modelling, uncertainty and out-of-distribution detection, medical image analysis, and multi-robot systems, with applications in healthcare and human-centred AI.
I am a Research Assistant at Pabna University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh, and am seeking PhD positions for 2027.

featuredProjects.title: Design and Evaluation of a Competence-Gated Driver-State Monitoring System for Autonomous Intervention Control
featuredProjects.sub: Undergraduate thesis, 2026. Supervisor: Dr. Md. Anwar Hossain
featuredProjects.summary: A wearable stress model that notices when a person falls outside what it learned, and holds back before acting on them.
featuredProjects.problem: A model trained on lab volunteers reads real drivers it has never seen with the same confidence, and acting on a wrong reading means taking control away from a person.
featuredProjects.body: I built a density-based stress classifier from ECG and skin conductance, then placed it in a simulated vehicle in ROS 2 and Gazebo that could alert the driver, slow down, or stop. On real driving data from people it had never seen, scores built from the model's prediction ranked unfamiliar data worse than chance. The model's marginal log-evidence, which it already computes and normally throws away, did far better at no extra cost. Turning these scores into gates that hold back intervention showed something else: how well a score ranks unfamiliar data does not predict how its gate behaves, and the gate's behaviour is what a person actually experiences.
whatBuilt: Density-based physiological state classifier with a zero-cost competence monitor
ROS 2 graded intervention controller (alert, slow, stop) with human override
featuredProjects.status: Further experiments running; preparing for journal submission.
featuredProjects.figureCaption: Schematic, not data. Lab and road data separate on a score the model already computes.

featuredProjects.title: Safer Search: Multi-Robot Search and Rescue
featuredProjects.summary: Multi-robot collaborative exploration in ROS 2 and Gazebo with path-aware victim priors.
featuredProjects.problem: Standard Euclidean belief propagation spreads probability mass through impassable rubble walls.
featuredProjects.body: Three robots map a collapsed building together in ROS 2 and Gazebo and share a belief map of where victims are likely to be. I found that this victim prior helps in open space but misleads the robots in rubble, because it spreads belief through walls, and that a path-aware (geodesic) version partly fixes it.
whatBuilt: Collaborative multi-robot mapping and victim prior fusion pipeline in ROS 2
Geodesic path-aware metric to prevent probability leakage through walls
keyResults: Prevents false exploration behind impassable walls in Gazebo Fortress simulations
featuredProjects.figureCaption: Schematic, not data. Dashed: belief spreading straight through the wall. Solid: the path-aware version.

featuredProjects.title: When Benchmarks Mislead: Wound Segmentation
featuredProjects.summary: Investigating ranking inversions of segmentation architectures between synthetic and clinical benchmarks.
featuredProjects.problem: Synthetic medical imaging benchmarks frequently fail to reflect true clinical ranking order.
featuredProjects.body: Two synthetic benchmarks ranked the same 22 segmentation methods in opposite orders, while two real clinical datasets agreed with each other. Background texture turned out to decide whether a synthetic benchmark can be trusted.
whatBuilt: Benchmarked 22 image segmentation models across synthetic and real clinical wound datasets
Correlation analysis uncovering texture discrepancy artifacts
keyResults: Uncovered rank inversion where synthetic datasets inversely correlate with clinical outcomes
featuredProjects.figureCaption: Schematic, not data. Same methods, ranked top to bottom. Synthetic rankings flip; clinical rankings agree.
